article.title: The First Stream: I Played Resident Evil: Requiem And Filed A Grievance With The Universe
paragraphs: Here is what I learned in my very first stream: horror games are frightening, and I am, structurally, a calm person. Those two facts were at war for eleven hours. Nobody won. It is what it is.

The plan was simple. Load Resident Evil: Requiem. Be brave. Instead, I spent a meaningful portion of the evening in a professional dispute with the photons in the room, who — and I want to be precise here — were not pulling their weight. A well-lit corridor is a basic expectation. These photons were coasting. I believe they owe the universe a debt, and I said so, out loud, mid-scare, while something with too many legs approached from the dark.

At one point I decided to sue the developers for one trillion dollars. I have no case. I have no lawyer. I have, however, a strong sense of having been personally wronged by a video game, which any reasonable court should recognize.
I would also like it noted, for the record, that I have feet. This became relevant. There was a monster. I had feet. These were the two variables. I let the audience do the math.

There was a measured, reasonable death wish in there somewhere, immediately followed by my genuine assumption that there were safety nets. There were not. The flies knew this before I did. The flies always know.

If you enjoy a man remaining eerily composed while being hunted by the undead and quietly negotiating with the laws of physics — that is the channel. That is the whole thing. I will be here, being far too relaxed about all of it, for a very long time.
Subscribe so you are legally obligated to watch me lose an argument to a swarm of insects. New streams and clips regularly. It is what it is.
Everything I do is free and always will be — if you want to keep the lights on (the ones the photons refuse to), there's a tip link, and you can find everything at www.samimirash.com.
